description: 2 tactical challenges for White against the Portuguese Variation. Meet 3...Bg4 with 4.Bb5+! or calm development.

drills.briefExplanation: 3.d4 Bg4 4.Bb5+! c6 5.dxc6 — check first, then win the pawn back with tempo.
drills.description: White to play. Black may try the Portuguese 3...Bg4 — play 3.d4 and know the check.
drills.explanation: The sharp antidote: after 3...Bg4, White plays 4.Bb5+! — checking and disrupting before Black consolidates. After 4...c6 5.dxc6 White wins the pawn back with tempo, Black's queenside is loosened, and the 'clever' pin only cost time. Against early pins, strike first.
drills.name: The Bb5 Check

drills.briefExplanation: 4.Nf3! e6 5.Bd3 Bd6 6.O-O — ignore the pin and develop; it will move.
drills.description: White to play. Black pinned with 3...Bg4 — develop calmly with 4.Nf3!.
drills.explanation: The calm antidote: 4.Nf3! simply develops, ignoring the pin — the bishop on g4 will have to move again. After 4...e6 5.Bd3 Bd6 6.O-O White is fully developed with the better center; Black's 'provocative' bishop achieved nothing but lost time. Don't panic at pins; develop through them.
drills.name: Developing Through the Pin
